messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: high error rate on /v1/stream (SSE) — 502s and tool-call parse failures. Customers affected: several active Dedicated tenants. Pager: alice. https://ops.redwood/logs/stream/2129 :rotating_light:

alice: on it. have we confirmed customer-visible errors? seeing 502s and reconnect storms in the dashboard.

jane: support: multiple customers reported truncated messages and 'invalid tool response' errors in their logs. one customer (acme-corp) reports client-side reconnect loop. raising to P1.

ben: thx. quick check: are we seeing SSE disconnects from the runtime or upstream? can someone paste the proxy/nginx logs and the runtime stderr?

carol: pasting s3 log link and brief timeline below. i grabbed the proxy tails.

``` 
proxy-logs tail -n 200 | grep stream
2129-03-15T18:01:02Z frontend nginx: 502 upstream prematurely closed connection at /v1/stream
2129-03-15T18:01:05Z frontend nginx: upstream sent partial chunk, client disconnected
2129-03-15T18:02:10Z frontend nginx: 200 OK /v1/stream
```

runtime stderr snippet (truncated):

```
2029-03-15T18:01:02.123Z ERROR svc.stream: stream write failed: write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->10.0.0.9:56312: i/o timeout
2029-03-15T18:01:03.001Z WARN svc.toolcall: parse_tool_response: json decode error: unexpected EOF
2029-03-15T18:01:03.002Z INFO svc.kvcache: evict prefix 0x1b2
```

ben: parse_tool_response unexpected EOF is interesting — suggests we received truncated JSON from the model runtime or that SSE framing split JSON objects across chunks and our parser isn't tolerant. any client-side changes?

alice: acme corp uses our JS SDK v0.9.1. @dave any compatibility notes for client-side chunk handling?

dave: JS SDK v0.9.1 uses incremental parsing that expects each tool-call payload as a full JSON object per message — we've had reports of newer model outputs using long text fields that cause the runtime to chunk mid-object. if a JSON object is split across multiple SSE events and the client parser expects a single event, that will error.

jane: customers seeing 'invalid tool response' in app logs. one attached log: `tool_result: "{\"status\":\"ok\",\"data\":{...` then abrupt EOF.

carol: high-level hypothesis list (working):
- H1: runtime emits SSE chunks that sometimes split tool-call JSON objects (framing issue)
- H2: proxy/nginx is closing connections prematurely due to perceived idle / backpressure (502s)
- H3: client SDK not robust to chunked JSON across SSE events (client compatibility)

ben: agreed. next steps: 1) gather full model->runtime logs around 18:01:00 2) extract a canonical truncated payload 3) validate parser behavior locally against split-chunk cases. i can own parser fix if it's our code.

alice: i'm going to escalate to dedicated infra. carol, can you coordinate status page + notify sales? jane, please draft customer-facing blurb. i'll do on-call handoff in 20m to ben.

carol: status page update: "Degraded streaming responses on /v1/stream causing truncated tool-call payloads for some customers. Engineers investigating. Mitigation: temporary increase in client reconnect backoff. ETA next update 30m." posting now.

jane: drafting: "We're investigating an issue affecting streaming responses which can cause tools integrated via function-calls to fail. If you see \"invalid tool response\" please retry, and contact support with trace-id. We're prioritizing customers on dedicated plans."

infra-bot: running canary mitigation: increasing nginx proxy send_timeout from 10s -> 60s for stream workers in eu-west-1. Command: `kubectl -n infra set configmap nginx-proxy --from-literal=send_timeout=60` — applying to canary nodes.

infra-bot: canary applied to node group canary-001, waiting 2m to observe.

ben: can someone paste a raw truncated payload we can use to reproduce? need exact bytes with SSE chunk boundaries.

carol: dropping one from logs (sanitized):

```
:event: message
data: {"type":"tool_call","tool":"search","payload":{"query":"list recent...","args":{

# << connection closed here >>
```

ben: perfect. i'll simulate an SSE stream that emits the JSON in two parts with a 50ms gap and run the current parser.

ben: local repro: parser throws `JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 312 (char 311)` when the object is split.

dave: that matches expectation. SDK v0.9.1 doesn't buffer across events. v1.0 (beta) uses an incremental combiner. can we ship a server-side mitigation so customers on older SDKs are protected?

ben: short-term mitigation options:
- M1: coalesce and ensure runtime always emits complete tool-call JSON in a single SSE event (fix in runtime, may require pipeline change)
- M2: enhance proxy to reassemble chunked messages before delivering to clients (hacky, edge cases)
- M3: encourage clients to upgrade SDK / provide temporary client patch (low adoption risk)
- M4: increase timeouts / buffering to reduce mid-object cuts (partial mitigation)

alice: what's quickest that reduces customer impact now?

carol: M4 + nginx send_timeout increase already applied to canary. if that materially reduces disconnects we'll roll it cluster-wide. also notify sales to recommend SDK upgrade to large customers.

ben: i'll open a runtime bug to prefer emitting full tool-call events when possible (H1 mitigation). patch is non-trivial but scoped — might be a few hours. will also prototype a tolerant parser fallback in the streaming gateway (fast to deploy).

ben: prototyping tolerant parser now — approach: assemble SSE data events into a buffer until a parse succeeds or buffer exceeds size X, then forward. will handle most split-object cases.

carol: timeline build (what we have so far):
- 18:00:57Z: first elevated 5xx alarms from frontend metrics
- 18:01:02Z: nginx logs show upstream premature close (502)
- 18:01:03Z: runtime stderr shows `json decode error: unexpected EOF` and `stream write failed: i/o timeout`
- 18:03:40Z: infra canary timeout increased, observe 18:04:10Z reduced 502s on canary
- 18:10:00Z: mitigation considered, engineering owner assigned (ben)

alice: i'm handing off to @ben for the RCA and follow through. i'm going offline for a few hours. ping me if we need escalation.

ben: taking over. i'll post an action tracker and link to a branch for the parser fallback.

ben: ACTIONS (initial):
- A1: runtime: add guard to prefer complete tool-call SSE events (owner: ben, ETA 6h)
- A2: streaming gateway: implement tolerant reassembly buffer and deploy (owner: ben, ETA 2h for prototype)
- A3: infra: roll nginx send_timeout cluster-wide if canary looks good (owner: carol, ETA 30m)
- A4: docs/devx: post advisory and recommended SDK versions + code snippet for robust parsing (owner: dave, ETA 1h)

jane: i'll send proactive messages to customers with known impact and include temporary workaround (increase SDK reconnect backoff & upgrade path).

carol: can we keep this thread focused on logs/timeline/hypotheses + mitigation status? i'll create an internal incident doc with details after handoff.

ben: reproducer gist: https://gist.redwood/repro/stream-split-json (private) — i'm pushing parser-fallback branch `fix/stream-reassembly`.

infra-bot: canary metrics: 502 rate on canary reduced from 12/min -> 1/min after send_timeout change. full rollout recommended.

carol: rolling nginx timeout change to other clusters now.

ben: deploying parser-fallback to staging. request code review from @dave @carol once CI passes.

dave: i'll update SDK docs and add example tolerant parser shim for older clients.

jane: customer comms sent to impacted accounts 18:28Z. support will escalate any severe regressions to this thread.

carol: postmortem note: please save all raw payloads + traces to /incidents/2129876543/artifacts before we purge logs.

ben: will collect and attach reproducer and instrumented traces. linking PR: https://git.redwood/p/fix/stream-reassembly.

alice: thanks all — leaving the incident in ben's hands. i'll be reachable if exec escalation needed. :white_check_mark:

(reacts in thread: :eyes: from dave, :thumbsup: from carol)
